title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Rao
release_notes: Add default autotune profiles for batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost
Introduce model quantization profiles and runtime selection heuristics (no automatic model-quality regression)
Add unit-economics tooling (CLI + API) and Console surfaces for per-route cost estimation
Safe rollout: new defaults guarded behind feature flag and gradual canary policy
description: Context: Customers running large production workloads asked for safer, opinionated defaults that improve unit economics without requiring manual tuning. This PR combines three tightly-related efforts: 1) sensible defaults and autotune heuristics for batching and prefix/KV caching, 2) first-class quantization profiles and runtime selection logic, and 3) developer tooling and Console surfaces to estimate unit economics per-route.
changes_summary: Summary of changes: (a) runtime: introduce BatchAutotuner and CacheHeuristics that pick default batch sizes and when to enable prefix KV caching based on request size distributions and SLO constraints; (b) quant: add quantization profiles (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) with validation hooks and a safety check that runs a lightweight eval to prevent quality regressions; (c) tooling: unit-econ CLI + backend endpoints and Console UI panels to show estimated cost/token and projected monthly spend under traffic; (d) config: add feature flag 'cost_autotune_defaults' and rollout policy for canarying; (e) docs + tests + perfbench updates.

ci_checks: perfbench: initial run failed (timing noise) -> rerun passed
benchmarks: Staging perfbench (g5.8x): average cost/token reduced by 9.3% across mixed chat+completion workload
P95 latency impact: +4ms on average (within SLO for majority of routes)
KV cache hit improvement: +12% for conversational workloads with frequent prefixes
migration_notes: Migration: The default changes are behind the 'cost_autotune_defaults' feature flag. Operators can opt-in per-route or per-tenant via Console or CLI. Quant profiles are additive and do not replace existing model artifacts; profile assignment is logged and reversible. Customers with strict quality requirements should run the provided sample-eval (tools/unit-econ/validate_profile) before enabling automatic profile selection.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: automatic quant selection could degrade output quality for edge-case prompts. Mitigation: require lightweight eval gate, gradual canary rollout (10%->50%->100%), and immediate rollback path with telemetry alerting. Also added gating metric to detect quality regression and revert automatically.
known_issues:
- Very large single-request batches (>32k tokens) may still bypass autotuner heuristics and fall back to manual config.
- Perfbench variability in some regions; we added a retry to CI for the perfbench step.
merge_details: Merged by Marisol Vega using squash merge. Commit message consolidated feature summary and listed migration steps. Rollout began immediately with a 10% canary and monitoring dashboards pinned to the Unit Econ panel.
notes_for_release_engineering:

- Coordinate with SRE to watch 'autotune.quality.regressions' and 'autotune.cost.delta' alerts during rollout.
- Tag cloud provider teams for potential kernel regression monitoring when enabling q8_0 on older GPU drivers.
